At the bottom intersection, the angle below the parallel line and on the right side of the slanted line is labeled 142°; at the top intersection, the angle above the parallel line and on the left side of the slanted line is labeled z°. In the middle there are also angles labeled (4x+6)° and (2y+8)°, but finding z does not require using them. Then reason: The top horizontal line and the bottom horizontal line are parallel, and the slanted line is a transversal. z and 142° are located on the outsides of the two parallel lines, and on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are a pair of alternate exterior angles. When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate exterior angles are equal, so z = 142.
